interface.title: TESS Target Pixels Inspector (tess_tpf_webapp)
interface.field: Astronomy: time-domain photometry, TESS exoplanet and variable-star vetting
interface.stage_of_work: Checking and vetting a signal after detection: deciding which star a periodic dip or variation comes from
interface.what_it_is_for: Enter a TIC ID, see the TESS target pixel file with nearby catalog sources overlaid, build light curves from chosen pixels, and compare with ZTF/ASAS-SN light curves to find out whether a variable signal comes from the target or a blended neighbour.

data.note: No built-in demo. Typed TIC 25155310, which downloaded its SPOC TPF from MAST (Sector 69, Camera 4.2). Also loaded the page's own example TIC 86263325 in Sector 49 (latest) and Sector 46 with mag. limit 14 (set through URL parameters tic/sector/magnitude_limit). Network access worked for MAST and the ZTF/IRSA archive. The SkyPatrol v2 and VSX queries always came back '(error)'. Gaia DR3 + TIC returned '(error)' for TIC 25155310 and drew no markers for TIC 86263325. The external light curves plotted and folded were of an arbitrary ZTF OID (1724108100002479) unrelated to either target and of a ZTF neighbour 61.8 arcsec from TIC 86263325; neither is the target itself.

tree.general: Decide whether a variable signal seen in survey photometry belongs to the target star or to a nearby blended source
tree.specific: Find out whether eclipses or dips in the TESS light curve of a TIC come from that star, using pixels, catalog overlays and ZTF light curves

features.name: Interactive aperture picker linked to light curve
features.general: Click, shift-click, ctrl-shift-click or box-select cells on an image grid to choose which pixels are summed; the time series redraws for the chosen set so you can compare the signal from different regions
features.specific: In Pixels Inspection, tap or Box Select pixels on 'Pixel data'; the 'Lightcurve for TIC' plot rebuilds from the selected pixels (normalized or in e/s, optional y min./max.)
steps: Press Inspect
Tap a pixel to replace the selection
Shift-click to add or Ctrl-Shift-click to remove pixels
Use Box Select to take a block
Compare the redrawn light curve (eclipses present or absent)
serves_tasks: Change which pixels are summed and see whether the signal follows the target or a neighbour
Make a light curve from the default aperture
Change the flux scaling and plot limits

features.name: Time scrubber linking light curve and image frame
features.general: Pick a moment in a time series with a slider, step buttons, or by clicking a point; a marker shows the chosen time and the image shows that frame

steps: Drag the Cadence Number slider
Click a point in an eclipse on the light curve
Step with < or >
Hover points for cadence details
serves_tasks: Step through time to see the image during an event

features.name: Per-pixel light-curve grid
features.general: Draw a small time series for every pixel of an image in a grid, with the current selection outlined, to see where a signal is spatially
features.specific: Per-Pixel Plot renders each pixel's light curve over the TPF footprint with the aperture in red; it warns when the time range is long
steps: Optionally zoom the light curve to a shorter time range
Press Per-Pixel Plot
Read which pixels show the dips
serves_tasks: See every pixel's own light curve on a grid

features.name: Image with survey-source overlay, hover and select details

screens_never_reached: Gaia DR3 + TIC source markers on the Skyview: the label went to '(error)' for TIC 25155310, and no markers appeared for TIC 86263325 in Sectors 49 or 46 after waiting about a minute (screens/031.webp, screens/054.webp, screens/068.webp)
VSX variable-star markers and classifications: the label always read 'VSX (error)'
ASAS-SN SkyPatrol v2 markers and SkyPatrol v2 links: the label always read 'SkyPatrol v2 (error)'
TESSCut fallback cutout (listed under Data sources): both targets had SPOC TPFs, so it was never triggered
not_done: Check VSX for existing variable classifications: the VSX query failed ('VSX (error)') on every target
Overlay Gaia DR3/TIC sources to identify contaminating stars by catalog: the overlay errored or never drew, so contamination was judged only from the pixel image and pixel light curves
Cross-match against ASAS-SN SkyPatrol v2: the query errored, so there was no SkyPatrol URL to plot; only ZTF was tested

The ZTF light curve plotted for TIC 86263325 is from a neighbour 61.8 arcsec away (the nearest ZTF match). The first ZTF plot and the P = 3.4 d fold (OID 1724108100002479) used an arbitrary ID unrelated to either target, only to exercise the panel. TIC 25155310 had 'ZTF (0)' matches. So no ZTF light curve of the target itself was compared, and no fold used a period taken from the TESS data.
No closing judgement was recorded: the run never weighed the aperture tests, the per-pixel grid and an external light curve together to say whether the signal comes from the target or a neighbour
Clicking the LC/snad/Zubercal, ExoFOP, Sector Visibility and centroid analysis links: they point off this server, so they were not followed; the LC URL was copied into the panel by hand
Screenshot 'Copy' button and the All / Pixels Inspection / External Lightcurve choices: only Skyview + Save was tried
Search box (Gaia DR3 Source, TIC ID): typing 25155310 and pressing Search had no visible effect, probably because the catalog it searches did not load
